questions.q: Which of the following matrices is equal to $6 \begin{bmatrix} -5 & 3 \\ 0 & -4 \end{bmatrix}$?
questions.explain: To multiply a matrix by a scalar (in this case, 6), you multiply every element inside the matrix by that scalar. Resulting entries: $6(-5) = -30$, $6(3) = 18$, $6(0) = 0$, and $6(-4) = -24$. This produces the matrix $\begin{bmatrix} -30 & 18 \\ 0 & -24 \end{bmatrix}$.
